validity.researcher_notes: Real project, well documented in Egyptian press across 2021-2023. Daily News Egypt (English, 2021-03-07) reported the minister inspecting a 120km line 'from the Amiriya area in Alexandria to New Alamein', cost EGP 2bn, feeding New Alamein's industrial/residential/tourist zones + a petrochemical complex, plus a separate 10km Borg El-Arab branch to Midor/Midalik -- confirming this is correctly classed as a gas transmission trunk (not gathering/plant-internal), confirming SegmentCost=2,000,000,000 EGP exactly, and confirming the Borg El-Arab-Midor spur is a genuinely separate line (matches GEM's existing separate row P6032, Borg El Arab-Midor Gas Pipeline len=10/dia=24) -- so no duplicate/double-count between P3931 and P6032. elmostqpalelyuom (Arabic, undated construction-phase article) independently gives 32in diameter, GASCO as implementer, EGP 540m interim cost estimate, and 68% progress with an expected Q3-2021 completion. dostor.org (2023-04-06) quotes GASCO's chairman announcing completion of 'khat ghaz al-Amiriya - al-Alamein al-jadida' at 170km/32in, explicitly as a line separate from the 10km/24in Borg El Arab-Midor spur -- this is the same article GEM's own wiki page cites for Status=Operating. Existing Fuel/PipelineType/Start refs (petroleum.gov.eg Mop_28122022_01, already in sheet) verified OK and are consistent (ministry's Dec-2022 year-end report lists a combined 'al-Amiriya/al-Alamein/Burg al-Arab' 130km project among 2022 completions).

validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL LENGTH DISAGREEMENT, does not resolve to a single number. (1) Daily News Egypt, 2021-03-07 (mid-construction): '120km long pipeline ... from Amiriya ... to New Alamein'. (2) Ministry of Petroleum year-end report (Mop_28122022_01.aspx, the sheet's existing Fuel/PipelineType/Start ref, Dec-2022): cites 130km for the combined 'al-Amiriya/al-Alamein/Burg al-Arab' project (GEM's current value matches this exactly). (3) dostor.org, 2023-04-06, quoting GASCO's own chairman announcing PROJECT COMPLETION: 'the al-Amiriya - New al-Alamein gas line project, 170km, 32in diameter' -- and explicitly treats the Borg El Arab-Midor spur (10km/24in) as a SEPARATE line, i.e. the 170km figure is NOT an omnibus total including the spur. This is the most authoritative source (direct company statement, issued after physical completion, specifically naming and disaggregating this exact line) and it disagrees with GEM's 130km by ~30%. GEM's own wiki page (checked 2026-07-13) already cites this same dostor.org article as ref [4] for Status=Operating, but the Length field on the wiki still shows the older 130km figure with no reconciliation -- i.e. GEM has been sitting on the 170km source without applying it to Length. Diameter (32in) is NOT in dispute -- both the mid-construction source and the completion source agree on 32in, matching GEM.

If the schema has a separate Operator field, populate it with GASCO; if not, consider noting GASCO in ResearcherNotes. Not urgent enough to block anything.
validity.researcher_notes: GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company) is the entity that built and operates this line per every source (dostor.org GASCO chairman statement, elmostqpalelyuom, Daily News Egypt). GASCO's own shareholding is EGAS 70% / Egypt Gas Co 15% / Petrojet 15% (per general company-profile search results, not specific to this pipeline) -- so GEM's Owner1=EGAS 100% overstates EGAS's direct stake in the operating company and omits GASCO as Operator entirely (Operator field is blank on the wiki page and not present among the audited value_cols). This is a common owner-vs-operator ambiguity flagged in the task brief; not independently a blocking concern given EGAS is genuinely the ultimate state parent, but worth a human look.

routes.corridor_desc: Runs WSW from the Amriya gas/industrial hub (SW Alexandria) along or near the Alexandria-Marsa Matruh coastal corridor (International Coastal Road / North Coast strip) to New Alamein City on the Mediterranean, per Daily News Egypt's description ('from the Amiriya area in Alexandria to New Alamein') and the Ministry of Petroleum's grouping of it with a Borg El Arab spur. No independently sourced intermediate waypoints were found (no GIS trace, no named intermediate towns beyond Borg El Arab, which belongs to the separate 10km spur/P6032, not this trunk) -- endpoints are reasonably well anchored (named city/district coordinates), but the exact path between them is not sourced beyond 'follows the coastal corridor'. Length disagreement (120-170km reported vs GEM's 130km) means the true routing could be less direct / more winding than a straight endpoint-to-endpoint line would imply.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoint coordinates are for the named places (Al-Amiriya district centroid; New Alamein city centroid, per public place-coordinate lookups), not for the pipeline itself -- no pipeline-specific coordinates were found or fabricated. Also note: the sheet's existing RouteNotes URL (masrawy.com, 2021/3/6) is truncated/malformed and returns HTTP 400 on verification -- it appears to be the Arabic-language report of the same March-2021 ministerial inspection Daily News Egypt covered in English, but the URL itself is broken and should be fixed or replaced, not relied on as-is.

summary: Real, correctly-classified transmission trunk (not a duplicate of the separate Borg El Arab-Midor spur P6032) with a material Length discrepancy (GEM 130km vs GASCO's own 170km completion announcement, which GEM's wiki cites for Status but never applied to Length) and a data-entry error on FuelSource (a URL sitting in the value cell); Diameter/Cost/Location/Construction/Status filled with verified refs, route suggested at low confidence (endpoints only, no waypoints).
